text:
Alex: quick async standup — what I did / blockers / today
Alex: did a short repro for the KV write-through race that pops up under high microbatch pressure. attached a small trace in the repo (see PR link below).
Maya: re: race — saw that locally too, fwiw. my debug run showed the eviction callback sometimes runs before the pending write ack lands.
Ryan: can you paste the minimal cmd you used to repro? I want to try on the tuning rig.
Alex: sure —
Alex: ```
# repro (run on a machine with ~4 concurrent clients)
PYTHONPATH=./eng_runtime tox -e bench -- micro_repro.py --batch-size=8 --prefetch=64 --warmup=200
```
Alex: results: p50 ~12ms, p95 ~210ms when race triggers, otherwise p95 ~48ms.
Carla: blocker: I hit a failing unit test in the kernel allocator after rebasing my batching PR — may be related to the eviction ordering. putting WIP on that PR.
Maya: pinging infra-bot to spin up a dedicated canary (small pool) to reproduce reliably in CI. @infra-bot canary request? :pray:
infra-bot: created canary-cluster-ax3 (2xA10g) in us-east-1, runs queued (job id: 44219).
Ryan: I'll run the repro there once it's up. if we confirm, we should try toggling `kv.prefetch` and `kernel.batch_slot_limit` to see the sensitivity.
Alex: tried quick sweep — prefetch 32 -> p95 ~120ms, prefetch 16 -> p95 ~85ms, prefetch 8 -> regression disappears but end-to-end throughput drops ~15%.
Carla: thanks — that's super helpful. for my allocator fix I can try to enforce write-ack order before eviction. small patch incoming.
Carla: opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-runtime/pull/8209 (WIP) — adds a simple barrier in KV write path and a unit test that simulates microbatch evict.
Maya: nice. can we also add a flaky e2e that reproduces on the canary so we don't regress? maybe gated with an env var.
Alex: yeah add a canary-only test harness, toggle with KVMICRO_REPRO=1.
Ryan: FYI I'm going to try a quick benchmark: baseline vs allocator-fix vs prefetch tweak. will drop results here.
SRE Oncall: FYI if the canary shows instability, set routing policy to fallback to smaller model variant to avoid customer impact.
Ryan: baseline (canary run): throughput 1.0x, p95 52ms. allocator-fix (local): throughput 0.98x, p95 55ms. prefetch=8: throughput 0.85x, p95 44ms.
Maya: looks like the allocator-fix trades a little throughput for stability — acceptable for Dedicated/Private defaults, but maybe add as opt-in knob for Hosted.
Alex: next steps: Carla lands allocator fix and unit test, Maya wires canary e2e, Ryan runs full sweep and posts perf table, I'll draft a short notes blurb for Console explaining the new knob and recommended defaults.
Carla: will aim to have PR ready for review by EOD.
Maya: I'll claim the canary test and coord infra-bot job.
Ryan: leaving a couple of review pings on related PRs. ping me when canary jobs finish. :thumbsup:
Alex: thanks all — nothing else from me. closing the loop later with numbers. :rocket:
